intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Interact with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated for generations, giving you an authentic taste of Tokyo's deep culinary heritage.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech and Anime District Deep Dive
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Tokyo's iconic electric town, visiting multi-floor electronics shops, retro gaming arcades, robot cafes, and cutting-edge gadget stores. Experience the intersection of otaku culture and consumer technology that defines modern Japanese innovation.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, strolling through the Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional crafts and snacks. Witness morning prayers, explore the five-story pagoda, and soak in centuries of Edo-period culture in one of Tokyo's most preserved historic districts.

experiences.name: Ramen Alley Tasting Experience in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Navigate the narrow, atmospheric lanes of Shinjuku's Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) and nearby ramen shops, tasting regional ramen styles from tonkotsu to shoyu. Sit elbow-to-elbow with locals at tiny counters and discover why Tokyo's ramen scene is considered among the world's finest.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Step into a world-renowned immersive digital art experience created by the art collective teamLab, featuring room-sized interactive installations that blend technology, nature, and human movement. This groundbreaking fusion of art and tech perfectly encapsulates Tokyo's avant-garde creative spirit.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita or Haneda Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Airport Limousine Bus or Keikyu/Narita Express train to your Tsukiji accommodation (approx ¥1,000–¥3,000 depending on airport). Check in, freshen up, and take a slow orientation walk around Tsukiji Outer Market — explore the narrow lanes, fish shops, and street food stalls that remain open in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Sumida River waterfront near Tsukiji for sunset views. Head to Tsukiji Outer Market area for a casual dinner — many small restaurants and izakayas cluster here offering fresh seafood bowls and grilled skewers at reasonable prices.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or convenience store (7-Eleven, FamilyMart) upon arrival — onigiri and sandwiches from ¥150–¥500
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market area izakaya or casual seafood restaurant — try a fresh tuna bowl (maguro don) for around ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Get a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport — it works on all trains, buses, and even convenience stores. Jet lag may hit; keep Day 1 light. Tsukiji Outer Market stalls typically close by 14:00–15:00 so you may catch the tail end.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (5:30–6:00) and visit Tsukiji Outer Market at its most vibrant — sample fresh tamagoyaki (rolled egg), grilled scallops, and tuna sashimi from market stalls. This is one of Tokyo's best free food experiences. Budget around ¥500–¥1,000 for tastings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 15 minutes to Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry) — a stunning traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond, tea house, and seasonal spring flowers. Afterward, take the inexpensive Tokyo Cruise water bus (¥800) from Hamarikyu up the Sumida River to Asakusa for a scenic and budget-friendly river journey.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Asakusa's Nakamise Shopping Street leading to the iconic Senso-ji Temple. The temple is free and beautifully lit at night. Browse souvenir shops for affordable omiyage (gifts). Dinner in Asakusa's backstreets.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market street food — tamagoyaki, grilled skewers, fresh sashimi bites (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Hamarikyu Gardens tea house — matcha and wagashi (traditional sweets) set for ¥510, or pack convenience store onigiri
meals.dinner: Asakusa backstreet restaurant — try menchi-katsu (deep-fried minced meat cutlet) or ramen for ¥700–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is best before 9:00 AM for freshness and atmosphere. Senso-ji is free to enter at all hours. The water bus is a scenic and affordable alternative to the metro — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Akihabara (Electric Town) — Tokyo's legendary tech and electronics district. Spend the morning exploring multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and Bic Camera, retro game shops, and anime merchandise stores. Window shopping is completely free and endlessly fascinating.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free floors of Akihabara's retro game shops and manga libraries. Check out the Akihabara Radio Kaikan building for vintage electronics and hobby goods. If budget allows, visit a maid café for the cultural experience (budget around ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a drink and the experience).
day_by_day.evening: Take the JR Yamanote Line to Ueno (5 minutes, ¥140). Visit Ueno Park at dusk — free entry, beautiful cherry blossom trees (late April may still have some blooms). Explore Ameyoko Market, a lively open-air market street with cheap street food, fresh produce, and clothing stalls.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast near hotel (onigiri + coffee) — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Akihabara — try a curry rice set lunch at a local restaurant or a gyudon (beef bowl) at Yoshinoya or Matsuya for ¥500–¥700
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market street food — grilled squid, takoyaki, fresh fruit, and cheap eats for ¥600–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is a must for tech culture enthusiasts. Many shops open around 10:00–11:00 AM. Ameyoko Market is busiest in the evening and is a fantastic budget dining spot. Ueno Park is free and great for people-watching.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Shibuya (approx ¥200 from Tsukiji area). Visit the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — the world's busiest pedestrian intersection. Explore Shibuya 109 (free to browse), and head up to the free Shibuya Sky observation deck alternative: the rooftop terrace of Scramble Square (¥2,000) OR the free view from Mag's Park rooftop at Shibuya Hikarie.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk uphill to Harajuku (15-minute walk or one train stop). Explore Takeshita Street for quirky youth fashion and affordable crepes (¥400–¥600). Then walk through the free and peaceful Meiji Jingu Shrine and its surrounding forested path — a perfect contrast to the commercial buzz.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Harajuku/Omotesando area and explore the backstreets (Ura-Harajuku) for free street style watching. Take the metro back to Tsukiji for a relaxed evening near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local bakery near Tsukiji — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Harajuku Takeshita Street — crepes, cotton candy, or a cheap ramen shop for ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Back in Tsukiji area — try a local sushi conveyor belt (kaiten-zushi) restaurant like Sushiro or Kura Sushi for ¥800–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Shibuya Scramble is iconic — try to experience it during both day and night. Meiji Jingu is free and serene. Saturday means Harajuku and Shibuya will be very crowded — embrace the energy! Kaiten-zushi chains are excellent budget-friendly options for sushi.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (old town) neighborhoods. Stroll through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, explore the historic Yanaka Cemetery (beautiful and peaceful), and browse independent craft shops and galleries. This area is almost entirely free to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to nearby Nezu Shrine — a smaller, less-crowded alternative to Fushimi Inari with a beautiful tunnel of torii gates. Free entry. Then explore the Yanesen (Yanaka-Nezu-Sendagi) area's independent coffee shops and local art studios.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koenji (30 minutes by metro, ¥200) for Tokyo's alternative culture scene — vintage clothing shops, independent record stores, and a laid-back local atmosphere very different from tourist areas. Great for budget dining at local izakayas.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza street food — freshly baked melon bread or croquettes from local shops for ¥150–¥300
meals.lunch: Local yoshoku (Western-Japanese fusion) restaurant in Yanaka — try an omurice or hamburg steak set for ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Koenji izakaya — order yakitori skewers and draft beer for ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is one of Tokyo's hidden gems — very few tourists, very local atmosphere. Nezu Shrine is far less crowded than Fushimi Inari in Kyoto and equally photogenic. Koenji has a strong music and subculture scene — look out for live music venues.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. Take the free Yurikamome Line scenic ride (or budget-friendly option: walk across Rainbow Bridge for free). Explore the teamLab Borderless digital art museum (book in advance, ¥3,200) OR skip it for budget reasons and explore the free outdoor areas, the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue, and the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza (free entry to the mall and Gundam area). Explore Palette Town and the futuristic architecture of Odaiba. The view of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline from Odaiba beach is completely free and stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Tokyo via Yurikamome Line. Head to Shimbashi — a classic salaryman district near Tsukiji. Explore the narrow izakaya alleys under the train tracks (Soto-Bori area) for some of Tokyo's most authentic and affordable after-work dining.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area convenience store or local café — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Odaiba food court in DiverCity or Aqua City mall — ramen, gyoza, or Japanese curry for ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Shimbashi izakaya alley — grilled chicken skewers, cold Sapporo draft, and edamame for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless is a world-class tech-art experience but costs ¥3,200 — worth it if budget allows. The Unicorn Gundam statue is free and a must-see for tech/anime culture fans. Shimbashi is extremely local and budget-friendly — one of Tokyo's best izakaya districts.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (approx 2 hours by budget Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa, ¥1,360 one way). Explore the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — ornate, gold-covered shrines and mausoleums in a cedar forest. Entry to the main area costs ¥1,300.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinno-ji Temple (¥400), walk the forested paths, and see the famous Shinkyo Sacred Bridge (free to view, ¥300 to walk across). The natural scenery and mountain air are a refreshing contrast to urban Tokyo.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Arrive back in Tsukiji area by 19:00–20:00. Enjoy a quiet dinner near the hotel — perfect for a relaxed evening after a full day trip.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before departing — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Nikko yuba (tofu skin) cuisine — a local specialty. Try a yuba soba set at a restaurant near the shrine for ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area — simple ramen or soba restaurant near the hotel for ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Book the Tobu Nikko Line in advance for the cheapest fare. A Nikko All Area Pass (¥4,520 round trip + unlimited buses) may be worth it if you plan to use buses. Start early — aim to leave Asakusa by 7:30–8:00 AM to maximize time in Nikko.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shimokitazawa — Tokyo's beloved bohemian neighborhood known for vintage shops, independent theaters, and live music. Browse the dozens of used clothing stores for budget fashion finds (items from ¥200–¥2,000). The neighborhood itself is free to explore and endlessly charming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Setagaya Literary Museum or explore Shimokitazawa's many independent bookshops and vinyl record stores. This area perfectly represents Tokyo's underground culture scene. Grab coffee at one of the many indie cafés.
day_by_day.evening: If budget allows, check out a live music show at one of Shimokitazawa's legendary small live houses (shimokita has dozens — entry typically ¥1,500–¥2,500 with one drink). Otherwise, enjoy dinner in the neighborhood and people-watch at the busy intersection.

meals.breakfast: Shimokitazawa indie café — pour-over coffee and toast set for ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Local curry restaurant in Shimokitazawa — the area is famous for its curry shops. A full curry meal costs ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa — small ramen shop or Japanese pub food at a local izakaya for ¥800–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Shimokitazawa is a 25-minute train ride from Tsukiji area (via Shinjuku, ¥200–¥250). It represents a completely different side of Tokyo — anti-commercial, creative, and very local. Wednesday evenings sometimes have cheaper live music entry fees.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the free Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku for panoramic 360-degree views of Tokyo from the 45th floor observation deck (free, opens 9:00 AM). On clear days you can see Mount Fuji. Afterward, explore Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500) — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's Kabukicho entertainment district (free to walk through), and visit the free Godzilla head on top of the Toho Cinema building. Browse Takashimaya Times Square and the underground shopping malls. Visit the Shinjuku Golden Gai area — a labyrinth of tiny bars, fascinating even in the daytime.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Shinjuku for dinner and evening atmosphere. Golden Gai comes alive at night — each tiny bar holds only 5–8 people and has a unique theme. Budget ¥1,000–¥2,000 for a drink and entry charge at one bar for a uniquely Tokyo experience.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel or local bakery — ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Shinjuku department store basement food hall (depachika) — grab bento boxes, onigiri, and prepared foods for ¥500–¥900
meals.dinner: Shinjuku Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — tiny yakitori stalls under the train tracks, smoky and atmospheric. Budget ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is completely free — one of the best budget views in Tokyo. Shinjuku Gyoen is worth the ¥500 entry. Golden Gai bars may charge a seating fee (¥500–¥1,000) — this is normal and part of the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Akihabara again with fresh eyes — this time focus on the retro tech and gaming culture. Visit the Super Potato retro game store (multiple floors of classic games and consoles), and the Akihabara Radio Kaikan for electronics components. Browse the free floors of Yodobashi Camera's massive tech complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kanda Myojin Shrine — a beautiful shrine that is the spiritual protector of Akihabara's tech industry. It holds regular IT company prayer ceremonies and sells digital-themed ema (prayer plaques). Free entry. Then explore Kanda's secondhand bookshop district (Jimbocho) — hundreds of used bookstores with English titles available.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Nihonbashi — Tokyo's historic commercial heart, just a short walk from Tsukiji. See the original Nihonbashi bridge (the zero-kilometer mark for all Japanese roads), and explore the elegant Coredo shopping complex. Dinner in the Nihonbashi area.

meals.breakfast: Local soba restaurant near Tsukiji for a traditional Japanese breakfast — morning soba set for ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Akihabara — try a Japanese-style hamburg steak (hambagu) lunch set at a family restaurant for ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Nihonbashi area — try a traditional tempura restaurant for a lunch-price dinner set (many offer discounted evening sets) for ¥1,000–¥1,500

day_by_day.notes: Kanda Myojin is a fascinating intersection of traditional Shinto culture and modern tech culture — unique to Tokyo. Jimbocho bookshops are a paradise for culture lovers and are entirely free to browse. Friday evening in Nihonbashi is lively with after-work crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line, ¥920 one way). Visit the iconic Great Buddha (Kotoku-in, ¥300 entry) and the surrounding temple grounds. Kamakura is a coastal town with over 65 temples and shrines — most with free or low-cost entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Daibutsu Hiking Trail (free) through bamboo groves and forested hills connecting multiple temples. Visit Hasedera Temple (¥400) with its stunning hillside garden and ocean views. Walk down to Kamakura beach for a free scenic break.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Arrive back in Tsukiji by 19:00. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the hotel — perhaps a final Tsukiji area seafood meal to celebrate being near the famous market.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — convenience store breakfast on the train ¥300–¥500
meals.lunch: Kamakura — try shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl, a local specialty, at a restaurant near Hase Station for ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area — treat yourself to a proper sit-down sushi restaurant for ¥1,500–¥2,000 as a near-end-of-trip celebration

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is best visited on weekdays but Saturday mornings are manageable. Arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds at the Great Buddha. The JR Pass (if purchased) covers the Yokosuka Line to Kamakura. Bring comfortable walking shoes for the hiking trail.

day_by_day.morning: Revisit any favorite neighborhoods or spots from the trip — use this as a flexible morning for last-minute exploration. Consider visiting Toyosu Market (the relocated wholesale fish market) — free observation decks allow you to watch the professional fish market in action. Book in advance via the official website (free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Final shopping and souvenir run — head to Don Quijote (Donki) in Roppongi or Shinjuku for budget-friendly Japanese snacks, cosmetics, and unique souvenirs. Everything is cheaper here than airport shops. Also check Daiso (¥100 shops) for affordable Japanese goods.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Tokyo — return to a favorite spot for a farewell dinner. Consider Ginza (a short walk from Tsukiji) for a splurge-worthy final meal, or keep it budget with a standing sushi bar (tachinomi) experience.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market breakfast — splurge slightly on a fresh sashimi breakfast set for ¥1,000–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Toyosu or nearby convenience store — keep it light and budget-friendly for ¥500–¥700
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner — standing sushi bar (tachinomi sushi) in Ginza or Tsukiji for ¥1,500–¥2,500 for a special final meal

day_by_day.notes: Toyosu Market tuna auction viewing requires advance registration (very limited spots, free). Don Quijote is open 24 hours — great for last-minute shopping. Pack your suitcase tonight to prepare for departure. Keep receipts for tax-free shopping refund at the airport (purchases over ¥5,000).

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo — wake up early for one last walk through Tsukiji Outer Market. Grab breakfast from the stalls and soak in the atmosphere one final time. Check out of the hotel and store luggage at a coin locker at the nearest train station (¥300–¥600 per locker).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — use remaining time for any last sightseeing. Ginza is a 10-minute walk from Tsukiji and has beautiful free street art installations and window shopping. Visit the free Itoya stationery flagship store for unique Japanese paper goods and design items.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport with plenty of time. Collect luggage from coin locker, proceed to Narita or Haneda Airport. Use remaining yen on airport food or duty-free shopping. Claim tax refunds on qualifying purchases before departing.

meals.breakfast: Final Tsukiji Outer Market street food — tamagoyaki, grilled scallop, and fresh tuna for ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Ginza area — a quick soba or udon restaurant for ¥600–¥900, or airport ramen before departure
meals.dinner: Airport or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. Narita Airport is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo; Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Coin lockers at Tsukiji Station or Shintomicho Station are convenient for luggage storage. Don't forget to convert remaining yen back to your home currency or spend at the airport.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use transit time to settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Narita/Haneda, clear customs, and take the airport express to central Tokyo. Check into your Tsukiji boutique hotel, freshen up, then take a gentle orientation walk through the Tsukiji Outer Market to get your bearings. Browse the stalls selling pickles, dried seafood, kitchenware, and street snacks as the afternoon vendors wind down.
day_by_day.evening: Ease into Tokyo with a relaxed dinner in Tsukiji. Explore the backstreets around Tsukiji Honganji temple, then stroll along the Sumida River waterfront for your first Tokyo night view. Early bedtime recommended to fight jet lag.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or convenience store snacks (7-Eleven onigiri, sandwiches) en route to hotel
meals.dinner: Tsukiji Outer Market area — try Sushi Zanmai or a local izakaya near the market for fresh sashimi sets (¥1,500–¥3,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless transit throughout the trip. Exchange some yen at the airport for convenience. April in Tokyo is cherry blossom season — expect crowds and beautiful scenery.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and visit Tsukiji Outer Market for a classic Tokyo breakfast experience. Watch tuna being sliced, sample tamagoyaki (sweet rolled egg), and sip green tea from market vendors. This is one of Tokyo's most authentic food culture moments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning Edo-period garden with a tidal pond, just a 10-minute walk from Tsukiji. Take a traditional tea ceremony at the garden's teahouse overlooking the water (¥500–¥800). Then take a short ferry up the Sumida River to Asakusa, passing under historic bridges.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Asakusa's Senso-ji Temple at dusk when the lanterns glow and crowds thin. Browse Nakamise Shopping Street for traditional crafts and souvenirs. Dinner in Asakusa's local dining scene.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sushi breakfast or tamagoyaki on a stick with miso soup (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from market stalls in Hamarikyu Gardens or a soba noodle shop near Asakusa (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Asakusa — Daikokuya Tempura (legendary tempura tendon since 1887) or a local izakaya on Hoppy Street (¥2,000–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens entry is ¥300. The Sumida River ferry (Tokyo Cruise) costs about ¥780 and offers great city views. Senso-ji is free to enter. Wear comfortable shoes for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Akihabara — Tokyo's legendary Electric Town and the epicenter of tech and otaku culture. Spend the morning exploring multi-floor electronics shops like Yodobashi Akiba, retro game stores, and component shops selling cutting-edge gadgets and rare tech finds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Dive deeper into Akihabara's subculture: visit a maid café for the quintessential experience (¥600–¥1,000 for a drink + performance), browse anime merchandise floors, and explore the Akihabara Radio Kaikan building — a tech-lover's paradise with floors of electronics, figures, and hobby shops.
day_by_day.evening: Head to nearby Kanda/Ochanomizu for dinner in a more local neighborhood, then return to the hotel via a pleasant evening walk through Nihonbashi — Tokyo's historic commercial heart with beautiful Meiji-era architecture lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or a local kissaten (traditional Japanese coffee shop) near Tsukiji for toast, egg, and coffee set (¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Akihabara — try a curry rice shop or ramen spot popular with locals (¥900–¥1,500). Curry is deeply embedded in Japanese tech-worker culture.
meals.dinner: Kanda area — Kanda Yabu Soba (historic soba restaurant, one of Tokyo's oldest) or a yakitori grill near Ochanomizu (¥2,000–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot — the main street and side alleys both have distinct characters. Free Wi-Fi is available throughout. Some maid cafés require reservations; walk-ins usually available on weekday afternoons.

day_by_day.morning: Visit teamLab Planets in Toyosu (book tickets in advance online, ¥3,200). This world-famous digital art immersive experience combines technology, nature, and culture in breathtaking installations. Go early to beat weekend crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Toyosu Market — the modern successor to Tsukiji's wholesale operations. Take the official market tour to see the famous tuna auctions (viewing area, pre-registration required) or simply explore the market building's restaurants and shops. Then walk along the Toyosu waterfront for views of Rainbow Bridge and the bay.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic artificial island. See the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue (free), browse DiverCity Tokyo Plaza, and enjoy the spectacular nighttime view of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline from the waterfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast or café near hotel before heading out (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Toyosu Market restaurant floor — fresh sushi or seafood bowl (kaisen-don) sourced directly from the market (¥1,500–¥3,000)
meals.dinner: Odaiba — try Decks Tokyo Beach food floor for a variety of Japanese cuisines, or a ramen shop with bay views (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets tickets must be booked online in advance — they frequently sell out, especially on weekends. Wear socks as shoes are removed inside. Odaiba is accessible via the scenic Yurikamome driverless monorail — worth the ride for the views.

day_by_day.morning: Take the train to Harajuku for the Sunday Takeshita Street experience — colorful fashion, crepe shops, and Tokyo's most expressive youth culture. Then walk through the serene Yoyogi Park, especially beautiful during cherry blossom season with locals picnicking under the trees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Meiji Jingu Shrine — a peaceful forested sanctuary in the heart of the city. Walk the gravel path through towering torii gates, observe traditional Shinto rituals, and browse the votive plaques. Then explore the upscale Omotesando boulevard — Tokyo's Champs-Élysées — with its striking architectural flagship stores.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Omotesando Hills and the backstreets of Aoyama for boutique shopping and gallery browsing. The area transitions beautifully into evening with well-lit cafés and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Marion Crêpes on Takeshita Street (a Tokyo institution) or a café in Harajuku (¥700–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Yoyogi Park picnic — grab bento boxes and drinks from nearby convenience stores or market stalls (¥800–¥1,200), or sit-down at a café on Omotesando
meals.dinner: Aoyama/Omotesando — try a Japanese-French bistro or a stylish izakaya in the backstreets (¥2,500–¥4,000). The area has excellent mid-range dining options.

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter. Yoyogi Park is especially lively on Sundays. Omotesando is excellent for window shopping even on a mid-range budget — the architecture alone is worth seeing. April cherry blossoms in Yoyogi Park may still be blooming.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Shinjuku for a full day of exploration. Start with the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free!) for panoramic city views — arrive early for the clearest skies and shortest wait.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's contrasting neighborhoods: the organized chaos of Kabukicho entertainment district by day, the peaceful Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry, stunning in cherry blossom season), and the narrow alleyways of Golden Gai and Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a cluster of tiny postwar bars and eateries.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Shinjuku at night — one of Tokyo's most electric experiences. Walk through the neon-lit streets of East Shinjuku, watch the famous Shinjuku scramble crossing, and explore the department store basement food halls (depachika) at Takashimaya or Isetan for incredible prepared foods.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or a standing soba/udon shop near Tsukiji station (¥500–¥800) — quick and delicious
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen area — a bento from a nearby konbini eaten in the garden, or a lunch set at a local teishoku (set meal) restaurant (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — yakitori skewers and cold beer in a tiny atmospheric stall (¥2,000–¥3,000 per person including drinks)

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building has two observation towers — the North Tower is usually open until 10:30 PM and is free. Shinjuku Gyoen is closed on Mondays — substitute with Shinjuku Central Park if so. Golden Gai bars are tiny (some seat only 6 people) and very welcoming to respectful tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko — a UNESCO World Heritage site about 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Nikko Line (¥1,360 one way or consider the Tobu Nikko Pass). Visit the lavishly decorated Toshogu Shrine complex, built in 1617 to enshrine Tokugawa Ieyasu, featuring intricate carvings and the famous three wise monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's sacred sites: Rinno-ji Temple with its giant golden Buddha statues, Futarasan Jinja Shrine, and the beautiful Shinkyo Bridge (Sacred Bridge) over the Daiya River. If time permits, walk up to Taiyuin Mausoleum — quieter and equally stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Arrive back in Tsukiji/Ginza area for a relaxed dinner close to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near Asakusa or Ueno station (en route to Tobu Nikko Line) — onigiri and coffee or a standing ramen shop (¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Nikko town — yuba (tofu skin) cuisine, a local specialty. Try a yuba soba or yuba kaiseki set lunch near the shrines (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji/Ginza area — a relaxed Japanese restaurant or a conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) chain like Sushiro or Hamazushi for affordable, quality sushi (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (by 8:00–8:30 AM) to maximize time in Nikko. The Tobu Nikko All Area Pass (¥4,780) covers round-trip train and buses within Nikko — excellent value. Nikko can be cold and misty in April — bring a light jacket. Toshogu entry is ¥1,300.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Ginza district — Tokyo's most prestigious shopping and cultural neighborhood, just a short walk from your Tsukiji hotel. Visit the Itoya stationery flagship store (9 floors of beautiful Japanese paper goods and design), browse the free gallery spaces in Ginza's art buildings, and admire the architecture of flagship stores by world-renowned architects.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Mori Art Museum or the National Art Center in nearby Roppongi (check current exhibitions — typically ¥1,800–¥2,000). Roppongi Hills also features the free Mori Tower observation sky deck lobby and excellent public art installations including Louise Bourgeois's iconic Maman spider sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Roppongi for the evening — the area transforms at night. Visit Tokyo Midtown's beautifully lit gardens, then enjoy dinner in the neighborhood before heading back to Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market morning routine — fresh fish breakfast or a traditional Japanese breakfast set at a nearby café (¥900–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Ginza — try the affordable lunch sets at upscale restaurants (many offer ¥1,000–¥2,000 lunch specials that would cost 3x at dinner). Ginza Six basement food hall is excellent for browsing.
meals.dinner: Roppongi — mid-range Japanese restaurant or an izakaya with good sake selection (¥2,500–¥4,000). The area has diverse options from yakitori to modern Japanese cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Many Ginza galleries and art spaces are free. The Itoya stationery store is a must for design and culture enthusiasts. Roppongi Hills and Tokyo Midtown are free to explore — only specific museum exhibitions require tickets. The walk from Tsukiji to Ginza takes about 15–20 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Borderless digital art museum in Azabudai Hills (new 2024 location — book tickets online, ¥3,800). A more expansive and exploratory experience than Planets, this is one of the world's most innovative intersections of technology, art, and culture. Allow 2–3 hours minimum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the new Azabudai Hills complex itself — a cutting-edge mixed-use development that represents Tokyo's vision of future urban living. Then head to nearby Minato ward to explore the Zojo-ji Temple with Tokyo Tower looming dramatically behind it — a perfect cultural contrast between ancient and modern.
day_by_day.evening: Climb Tokyo Tower (¥1,200 for main deck) at dusk for spectacular views as the city lights up. The tower is smaller and more intimate than Skytree, with a nostalgic Showa-era charm. Return to Tsukiji for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Local kissaten (retro Japanese coffee shop) near hotel — morning set with toast, boiled egg, and coffee (¥600–¥900)
meals.lunch: Azabudai Hills food hall or a nearby café — the complex has excellent mid-range dining options representing various Japanese regional cuisines (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Tsukiji area — try a different restaurant in the neighborhood, perhaps a yakitori spot or a small ramen shop you noticed earlier in the trip (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless tickets must be booked well in advance online. Zojo-ji Temple is free to enter and the garden behind the temple has hundreds of Jizo statues — a moving and photogenic sight. Tokyo Tower's observation deck is best visited at dusk for both daytime and nighttime views.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Walk through Yanaka Cemetery (beautiful in cherry blossom season), browse the Yanaka Ginza shopping street with traditional craft shops and local food stalls, and feel the atmosphere of old Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Ueno museum district. Visit the Tokyo National Museum — Japan's largest museum with an extraordinary collection of Japanese art, samurai armor, ceramics, and ancient artifacts (¥1,000). The museum grounds also include a beautiful Japanese garden open seasonally.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ueno's Ameyoko Market — a lively open-air market street with food stalls, fresh produce, discount goods, and street food. The evening atmosphere is especially vibrant on Fridays. Then enjoy dinner in the area before returning to Tsukiji.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka Ginza — freshly made melon pan (sweet bread) from a local bakery, or a traditional Japanese breakfast at a small café in the neighborhood (¥700–¥1,200)
meals.lunch: Ueno area — try a tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) restaurant or a yoshoku (Japanese-Western fusion) restaurant near the museum (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market area — fresh seafood skewers, gyoza, or grab various street foods for a casual market dinner (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored slowly on foot — allow at least 2 hours. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. Ameyoko is busiest and most atmospheric on weekday evenings and weekends. The Yanaka–Nezu–Yanesen area is excellent for authentic Tokyo photography.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura — about 1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line. Start with the iconic Kotoku-in Great Buddha (Daibutsu) — a 13-meter bronze Buddha dating from 1252. Then walk the coastal Daibutsu Hiking Trail through bamboo groves and forested hills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kamakura's temple circuit: Hase-dera Temple with its stunning hillside garden and sea views, Zeniarai Benzaiten Shrine (wash your money in the cave spring for good fortune), and the charming Komachi-dori shopping street for local crafts, matcha sweets, and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo in the early evening. Stop at Yokohama's Chinatown (en route) if time permits for a quick exploration of Japan's largest Chinatown. Back in Tsukiji, enjoy a final evening walk along the Sumida River.

meals.breakfast: Early departure — grab onigiri and coffee from a convenience store or a quick breakfast near Tsukiji before heading to the train (¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Kamakura — shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl at a restaurant near Hase-dera, a local specialty unique to the Kamakura/Enoshima coast (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Yokohama Chinatown (if stopping) for dim sum or Chinese BBQ, or back in Tokyo at a mid-range restaurant near the hotel (¥2,000–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 8:00–8:30 AM. JR Pass holders can use it for the Yokosuka Line. Kamakura's Great Buddha entry is ¥300. Hase-dera entry is ¥400. April weather in Kamakura is mild and pleasant — the temple gardens may have late cherry blossoms or wisteria beginning to bloom. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the hiking trail.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tokyo Skytree — Japan's tallest structure at 634 meters. Book tickets online in advance (¥2,100 for Tembo Deck at 350m, or ¥3,400 including the Tembo Galleria at 450m). The views on a clear morning are extraordinary, extending to Mt. Fuji on good days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Skytree's base area — Solamachi shopping complex has excellent food, traditional craft shops, and a planetarium. Then cross to nearby Kappabashi Dori — Tokyo's wholesale kitchenware street, a fascinating cultural experience where you can buy professional Japanese knives, lacquerware, ceramics, and the famous plastic food models.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Tokyo — return to Asakusa for a nostalgic last stroll through Senso-ji at night. The illuminated temple and pagoda are magical. Celebrate your final night with a special dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Solamachi food hall at Skytree base — excellent Japanese breakfast options including regional specialties from across Japan (¥1,000–¥1,800)
meals.lunch: Kappabashi/Asakusa area — a traditional tempura or unagi (eel) restaurant for a quintessential Tokyo lunch (¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a kaiseki-style set meal or a high-quality sushi counter near Ginza/Tsukiji (¥4,000–¥7,000 per person). This is the meal to remember Tokyo by.

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Skytree tickets sell out on weekends — book online at least a few days ahead. Kappabashi Dori is a must for food culture enthusiasts — the Japanese knife shops in particular are world-class. Pack any purchases carefully. Begin thinking about what to pack and what to leave — luggage forwarding services (takkyubin) can send bags to the airport from convenience stores.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tsukiji — one last breakfast at the Outer Market, saying goodbye to the vendors and flavors that bookended your trip. Do any last-minute souvenir shopping: the market area has excellent Japanese kitchen tools, teas, and food gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of hotel (standard checkout 11:00 AM — confirm with hotel). Store luggage if your flight is later. Take a final walk through Ginza or a nearby neighborhood. Visit a depachika (department store basement food hall) at Mitsukoshi or Matsuya in Ginza for beautifully packaged Japanese food souvenirs and sweets to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport. Allow 2–2.5 hours before departure. Narita: take Narita Express (N'EX) from Shinjuku or Tokyo Station (~¥3,070, ~60 min). Haneda: take Tokyo Monorail from Hamamatsucho or Keikyu Line from Shinagawa (~¥700, ~30 min).

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — final fresh sushi breakfast or tamagoyaki with miso soup. Make it count. (¥1,000–¥2,000)
meals.lunch: Ginza depachika food hall — assemble a beautiful bento-style lunch from various stalls, or sit at a counter restaurant for a final ramen or soba bowl (¥1,000–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Narita or Haneda — both airports have excellent Japanese restaurant options including ramen, sushi, and tonkatsu at fair prices (¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Redeem any remaining Suica/Pasmo balance at the airport or keep the card for a future visit (cards are valid for 10 years). Declare any food items when returning home — many Japanese food products are permitted but rules vary by country. Keep receipts for tax refund claims (tax-free shopping requires passport at purchase). Sayonara, Tokyo!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the bustling Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street snacks from legendary vendors. Interact with local fishmongers and food artisans who have operated for generations, giving you an authentic taste of Tokyo's deep culinary heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Narita/Haneda Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to boutique hotel in Tsukiji, Chuo City. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your premium accommodations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the Tsukiji Outer Market neighborhood. Browse the iconic stalls of the Outer Market, sampling fresh tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, and premium sushi bites from renowned vendors. Pick up artisan snacks and get acquainted with the vibrant local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a celebrated Tsukiji-area sushi counter — opt for an omakase experience at a high-end sushi restaurant such as Sushi Saito (reservation essential) or a local chef's table near Ginza for a curated multi-course introduction to Tokyo's finest seafood.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: Light bites at Tsukiji Outer Market stalls upon arrival (tamagoyaki, fresh uni, oysters)
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi dinner at a premium Tsukiji or Ginza sushi counter (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Jet lag may be a factor — keep the first evening relaxed. Confirm omakase reservation well in advance. Private airport transfer recommended for a seamless luxury arrival experience.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the authentic Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — explore the bustling market with a knowledgeable local guide, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, Japanese pickles, dashi broth, and rare street snacks from legendary vendors. Learn the history and culture of Japan's most iconic food market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to nearby Ginza for an afternoon of luxury cultural immersion. Visit the Itoya flagship stationery and design store (a Tokyo institution), explore the Ginza Six complex featuring curated Japanese art installations, and browse flagship boutiques. Visit the Shiseido Gallery for contemporary art.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ginza Kojyu or Quintessence — a Michelin-starred kaiseki or French-Japanese fusion restaurant offering an extraordinary multi-course tasting menu showcasing seasonal Japanese ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Fresh sushi and tamago breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market during the food tour
meals.lunch: Refined tempura lunch at Tempura Kondo or Mikawa Zezankyo in Ginza
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred kaiseki or tasting menu dinner in Ginza (¥40,000–¥80,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Tsukiji Outer Market is most vibrant before 9:00 AM — start the food tour at 7:00–8:00 AM for the best experience. Ginza shops typically open at 11:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Hamarikyu Gardens, a stunning Edo-period landscape garden just minutes from Tsukiji. Stroll through meticulously maintained traditional gardens, tidal ponds, and seasonal cherry blossom or spring foliage. Enjoy a traditional matcha tea ceremony in the historic teahouse overlooking the garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a scenic water bus from Hamarikyu to Asakusa. Explore Senso-ji Temple, Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Walk the Nakamise shopping street for premium Japanese crafts, lacquerware, and traditional sweets. Visit the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center rooftop for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Asakusa Imahan or Onyasai — premium sukiyaki or shabu-shabu with Wagyu beef in a traditional setting with impeccable service and private dining rooms.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast at the hotel or a local kissaten (coffee shop) serving morning sets
meals.lunch: Traditional soba lunch at Kanda Yabu Soba or Sometaro in Asakusa
meals.dinner: Premium Wagyu sukiyaki or shabu-shabu at Asakusa Imahan (¥20,000–¥35,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hamarikyu Gardens open at 9:00 AM. Water bus tickets can be purchased at the garden's pier. Book the sukiyaki dinner in advance — private rooms fill quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Full immersion in Tokyo's tech culture — visit Akihabara Electric Town. Explore multi-floor electronics megastores (Yodobashi Camera, Bic Camera), cutting-edge gadget shops, and Japan's renowned anime and gaming culture. Visit the Akihabara Radio Kaikan for rare tech collectibles and retro electronics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the teamLab Planets digital art museum in Toyosu (advance booking essential). Experience immersive, boundary-pushing digital art installations that blur the line between technology and culture — one of Tokyo's most extraordinary premium experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium restaurant in Toyosu or Shiodome — consider the Michelin-starred Sazenka for extraordinary Chinese-Japanese fusion, or dine at a high-altitude restaurant in the Shiodome Caretta building with spectacular Tokyo skyline views.

meals.breakfast: Artisan bakery breakfast at Maison Landemaine or similar premium bakery near Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Ramen at a premium Akihabara ramen shop or a quick Japanese curry at a local specialist
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred dinner or premium skyline restaurant in Shiodome (¥25,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets tickets must be booked online well in advance — extremely popular. Akihabara is busiest on weekends — arrive early for a more comfortable experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Nezu Museum in Aoyama — a world-class museum housing an exceptional collection of pre-modern Japanese and Asian art, including ceramics, lacquerware, and textiles. The museum's stunning traditional garden is a serene highlight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Omotesando — Tokyo's most elegant boulevard. Visit flagship architecture-forward stores (Prada by Herzog & de Meuron, Louis Vuitton, Dior). Browse the Omotesando Hills complex for Japanese designer brands. Detour into Harajuku's Ura-Harajuku for avant-garde fashion and culture.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Florilège or L'Effervescence — two of Tokyo's most celebrated contemporary French-Japanese restaurants offering exceptional tasting menus with innovative seasonal ingredients and impeccable wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Luxury hotel-style Japanese or Western breakfast set near Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at Omotesando Hills restaurant or a refined café in the Aoyama area
meals.dinner: Contemporary French-Japanese tasting menu at Florilège or L'Effervescence (¥35,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Nezu Museum is closed on Mondays — Sunday visit is ideal. Book dinner at Florilège or L'Effervescence at least 2–3 months in advance as they are among Tokyo's most sought-after reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Imperial Palace East Gardens — explore the historic grounds of the former Edo Castle, including ancient stone walls, traditional Japanese landscaping, and seasonal spring flowers. The East Gardens are open to the public and offer a profound sense of Tokyo's imperial heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Modern Art (MOMAT) in Kitanomaru Park — Japan's premier modern art museum with an outstanding collection of 20th-century Japanese paintings, prints, and crafts. Afterward, stroll through Kitanomaru Park and cross the iconic Nijubashi Bridge.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Nihonbashi Yukari — a renowned three-Michelin-starred kaiseki restaurant in the historic Nihonbashi district, offering exquisite traditional Japanese cuisine in an elegant setting.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Japanese breakfast (gohan, miso shiru, grilled fish) at a local teishoku restaurant near Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Premium bento or Japanese cuisine at a refined Marunouchi restaurant near the Imperial Palace
meals.dinner: Three-Michelin-starred kaiseki at Nihonbashi Yukari (¥40,000–¥70,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Imperial Palace East Gardens are closed on Mondays and Fridays — check current schedules. Nihonbashi is a 10-minute taxi from Tsukiji — very convenient for returning to the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Yanaka — one of Tokyo's most beautifully preserved old shitamachi (downtown) neighborhoods. Explore the historic Yanaka Cemetery (stunning during spring), the Yanaka Ginza shopping street, ancient temples, and traditional wooden machiya townhouses. A rare glimpse of pre-war Tokyo culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to nearby Nezu and Yanesen district. Visit the Nezu Shrine with its iconic rows of red torii gates (a less crowded alternative to Fushimi Inari). Browse artisan workshops, pottery studios, and independent galleries in this culturally rich neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tsukiji area for dinner at Sushi Yoshitake or a comparable three-Michelin-starred sushi counter in the Ginza area — an intimate, world-class omakase experience with premium seasonal fish.

meals.breakfast: Artisan coffee and fresh pastry at a specialty café near the hotel
meals.lunch: Traditional menchi katsu (deep-fried minced meat cutlet) and local street food at Yanaka Ginza
meals.dinner: Three-Michelin-starred omakase sushi in Ginza (¥35,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is approximately 30 minutes from Tsukiji by subway. Wear comfortable walking shoes — the neighborhood involves significant walking on cobblestone streets. A wonderful day for photography.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's most prestigious contemporary art museums with rotating world-class exhibitions. Combine with the Tokyo City View observation deck for sweeping 360-degree panoramas of the Tokyo skyline, Mount Fuji (weather permitting), and Tokyo Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Roppongi's remarkable concentration of world-class museums — visit the National Art Center Tokyo (the largest exhibition space in Japan) and the Suntory Museum of Art in Tokyo Midtown, which houses an exquisite collection of Japanese decorative arts. Stroll through Tokyo Midtown's curated shops and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ryugin — one of Japan's most celebrated and innovative kaiseki restaurants, where Chef Seiji Yamamoto reinterprets traditional Japanese cuisine through a modern scientific lens. A truly once-in-a-lifetime dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Luxury breakfast at the hotel or a premium café near Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Refined lunch at a Roppongi Hills restaurant — try the Japanese restaurant Keyakizaka for a premium set lunch
meals.dinner: Michelin-starred innovative kaiseki at Ryugin (¥50,000–¥80,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Ryugin 2–3 months in advance — it is one of Tokyo's most difficult reservations. The Mori Art Museum is open late (until 22:00 on most days), offering flexibility. Tokyo City View is best at dusk for spectacular golden hour views.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided experience at the Sony Innovation Studio or Panasonic's Wonder Life-BOX innovation center — a deep dive into Japan's extraordinary tech culture, showcasing cutting-edge robotics, AI, smart home technology, and future-forward consumer electronics. An exclusive behind-the-scenes look at Japanese technological innovation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic waterfront island. Explore the teamLab Borderless digital art museum (if not already visited), the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) featuring ASIMO robots and space exploration exhibits, and the iconic Rainbow Bridge views.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premium Odaiba waterfront restaurant or return to Ginza for dinner at Sushi Saito — widely considered among the finest sushi restaurants in the world, offering an unparalleled omakase experience (reservation through concierge only).

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast teishoku near Tsukiji
meals.lunch: Casual but quality ramen or udon at a premium Odaiba restaurant with Tokyo Bay views
meals.dinner: World-class omakase sushi or premium seafood dinner (¥40,000–¥80,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan robot demonstrations are scheduled at specific times — check the schedule in advance. Odaiba is accessible by the scenic Yurikamome monorail from Shimbashi — a fun and futuristic transit experience in itself.

day_by_day.morning: Day excursion to Nikko — a UNESCO World Heritage Site approximately 2 hours from Tokyo by Shinkansen and local train. Explore the extraordinarily ornate Tosho-gu Shrine complex, dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu, surrounded by ancient cedar forests. Marvel at the Yomeimon Gate's intricate carvings and gold leaf detailing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko's cultural treasures — visit Rinnoji Temple, the serene Shinkyo Sacred Bridge over the Daiya River, and the Taiyuinbyo Mausoleum. If time permits, take a short bus ride to the stunning Kegon Waterfall and Lake Chuzenji for breathtaking natural scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Dinner at a premium teppanyaki restaurant — Ukai-tei in Ginza offers world-class Wagyu beef teppanyaki with theatrical tableside preparation in an elegant, intimate setting.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure to Nikko
meals.lunch: Traditional yuba (tofu skin) cuisine at a Nikko specialty restaurant — a regional delicacy unique to the area
meals.dinner: Premium Wagyu teppanyaki at Ukai-tei Ginza (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Depart early (7:00–8:00 AM) to maximize time in Nikko. Purchase the Nikko World Heritage Pass for convenient access to multiple sites. The Romancecar or Tobu Nikko Limited Express offers a comfortable premium train experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno — Japan's oldest and largest museum, housing the world's most comprehensive collection of Japanese art and antiquities. Highlights include samurai armor, ancient pottery, Buddhist sculptures, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. Arrange a private curator-guided tour for an in-depth premium experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ueno Park and its cultural institutions — visit the Tokyo Metropolitan Museum of Art for rotating contemporary exhibitions, stroll through the park's cherry blossom paths, and browse the Ameyoko Market for a lively contrast of street culture and local shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Japanese performing arts experience — reserve premium seats at the Kabukiza Theatre in Ginza for a Kabuki performance (English audio guides available), or arrange a private Noh theatre performance through your hotel concierge for an intimate cultural encounter.

meals.breakfast: Artisan coffee and premium Japanese pastry near the hotel
meals.lunch: Refined kaiseki lunch at Ueno Seiyoken — a historic French-Japanese restaurant in Ueno Park dating back to 1872
meals.dinner: Post-theatre premium dinner at a Ginza restaurant — try Ginza Kojyu for exquisite kaiseki (¥30,000–¥50,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Kabukiza Theatre performances can be long (4–5 hours for full programs) — single-act tickets are available for shorter visits. Book premium Kabuki seats through your hotel concierge well in advance. The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Private tea ceremony and cultural workshop experience — arrange a premium private session with a tea master in a traditional machiya setting, learning the philosophy and precise ritual of the Japanese tea ceremony (chado). Follow with a calligraphy or ikebana (flower arranging) workshop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shibuya and Shinjuku — experience the iconic Shibuya Crossing (the world's busiest pedestrian intersection), visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck for panoramic views, and explore the innovative Shibuya Stream and Scramble Square developments showcasing Tokyo's urban tech culture.
day_by_day.evening: Final premium dinner experience — reserve at Sazenka (Michelin three-star Chinese-Japanese fusion in Minami-Azabu) or return to a favorite restaurant for a farewell omakase. Conclude the evening with drinks at a rooftop bar — the Park Hyatt Tokyo's New York Bar (Lost in Translation fame) offers an iconic and memorable nightcap.

meals.breakfast: Luxury Japanese breakfast at the hotel
meals.lunch: Premium tonkatsu at Butagumi in Nishi-Azabu — Japan's finest pork cutlet using heritage-breed pork
meals.dinner: Michelin three-star farewell dinner followed by cocktails at the New York Bar, Park Hyatt Tokyo (¥50,000–¥90,000 per person for dinner)

day_by_day.notes: Book the private tea ceremony experience through your hotel concierge — several premium providers offer exclusive sessions in traditional settings. The New York Bar has a cover charge on evenings with live jazz — reserve a window table in advance for the best views.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tsukiji — one last leisurely walk through the Tsukiji Outer Market for breakfast sushi and a farewell cup of dashi broth. Pick up premium Japanese food souvenirs: aged soy sauce, artisan dashi packets, premium matcha, and seasonal wagashi sweets. Visit Ginza for last-minute luxury shopping — Japanese whisky, ceramics, or lacquerware.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, visit the Intermediatheque — a remarkable free museum in the KITTE building near Tokyo Station, showcasing the University of Tokyo's extraordinary natural history and cultural collections in a beautifully designed space. Browse the KITTE Marunouchi food hall for premium Japanese food gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport. Enjoy premium airport lounge facilities before departure — Tokyo's international airports offer exceptional lounge experiences with Japanese cuisine and sake. Depart Tokyo with extraordinary memories of a world-class journey.

meals.breakfast: Fresh sushi and Japanese street food farewell breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market
meals.lunch: Premium bento or a final Japanese set meal at a Marunouchi or KITTE restaurant
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or an early dinner at a premium restaurant near Tokyo Station before transfer

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for airport transfer and check-in. Japanese customs regulations restrict certain food items — check guidelines before purchasing food souvenirs. Consider shipping larger purchases home via Japan Post's reliable takuhaibin delivery service.
